about.introDesc: Go Nurture Initiative CIC is an asset-locked Community Interest Company (CIC) and the social impact arm of Nurtured & Nourished Women's Health Ltd. We deliver free, referral-led, culturally adapted perinatal education, infant feeding and community support to Black, Asian, Minority Ethnic, and displaced women across Norfolk.
about.missionDesc: Every mother deserves access to high-quality perinatal support, regardless of her background, immigration status, or financial situation. We exist to bridge the gap between traditional maternity services and the women who are too often left behind.
about.howDesc: A portion of profits from our commercial parent company — Nurtured and Nourished Women's Health Ltd — is transferred through Corporate Social Responsibility to fund the free community programmes delivered by Go Nurture Initiative CIC. This ensures financial sustainability while keeping services completely free for the women who need them.
about.pilotDesc: Our pilot programme will support 30 vulnerable women across three annual cohorts. Each cohort will receive culturally adapted perinatal education, birth preparation, and postnatal support — all delivered in a safe, welcoming, and multilingual environment.
about.referralDesc: Access to our programmes is through verified referral partners only — including NHS teams, local midwives, health visitors, English Plus, Bridge Plus, New Routes, community churches, and mosques. This ensures every woman is connected to the support she needs through trusted professionals.
about.valuesIntro: These are the values that guide both our companies. For our CIC, this is how we live them in partnership with Norwich's faith and community organisations.
about.faithCore: Faith grounds the enterprise's purpose, integrity and respect for the beliefs, cultures and spiritual identities of the women it serves.
about.faithCicContext: In our CIC, we partner with churches, mosques, temples and faith leaders across Norwich. We respect every woman's beliefs and work through trusted faith communities to reach pregnant BAME and Displaced women with free, culturally safe support.
about.growthCore: Growth drives continuous learning, excellence, innovation, evidence development and the creation of new programmes, services and intellectual property.
about.growthCicContext: In our CIC, this means we created our free 7-week perinatal education programme and infant feeding clinic, shaped by feedback from the women and communities we serve, to fill real gaps in care.
about.relationshipsCore: Relationships shape how the enterprise builds trust, strengthens communities and works with women, families, professionals, commissioners and partner organisations.
about.relationshipsCicContext: In our CIC, we build trusted referral pathways with different organisations and groups. Through these relationships, organisational leaders can refer women directly to our free programmes so no one falls through the cracks. We also try to strengthen relationships around women through ensuring deeper understanding of roles and boundaries of individuals surrounding the birthing person.

about.teamQuote: We are mums, clinicians, and community members. We built this for us, by us.
about.member1Bio: Registered Nurse, Antenatal Educator, and Trainee Lactation Consultant. A mum of 2 with lived experience of navigating maternity and infant feeding in the UK. Favour founded the CIC to ensure women from BAME and Displaced communities get free, culturally sensitive perinatal education and feeding support. She also volunteers as a Breastfeeding Peer Supporter with Breastfeeding Support Norfolk and Norwich.
about.member2Role: Certified Lactation Specialist & Director, Breastfeeding Support Norwich & Norfolk
about.member2Bio: Marion is a Certified Lactation Specialist, Breastfeeding Counsellor and Mindful Breastfeeding Practitioner, and Director of Breastfeeding Support Norwich & Norfolk. She offers warm, evidence-based breastfeeding and lactation support to families across Norwich and Norfolk, whether that's working through a tricky latch, navigating pumping, or just having someone to sit with you and listen without judgement. She's passionate about supporting families and committed to inclusive, culturally sensitive care, and she is honoured to support Black mothers as part of this community.
about.member3Bio: Qualified Accountant and mum of 2. Amarachi brings financial oversight and strategic governance to ensure the CIC is sustainable and transparent. She is passionate about creating equitable access to health support so that every mother, regardless of background, can thrive.
about.member4Bio: Cybersecurity Analyst and mum with lived experience. Christianah brings expertise in data protection, digital safety, and systems thinking to the board. She is committed to building safe, accessible services that empower women from underserved communities with knowledge and confidence.
about.member5Bio: Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife. Abimbola is deeply passionate about maternal health and advocating for women from BAME and Displaced backgrounds. She brings clinical expertise and a warm, culturally aware approach to our perinatal education, helping women feel seen, heard, and supported.
about.member6Bio: Registered Nurse with a heart for community health. Grace is passionate about breaking down barriers to care for women in our target communities. She supports the delivery of our free education and feeding support, ensuring every woman receives practical help with dignity and respect.

programmes.introDesc: Our programmes are designed specifically for vulnerable, Minority Ethnic, migrant, refugee, and displaced women. All sessions are free, referral-led, and delivered in a safe, welcoming, and multilingual environment.
programmes.cohortsDesc: Each year, we run three cohorts of our community perinatal programme. Each cohort supports up to 10 women through a comprehensive journey of education, preparation, and postnatal care.
programmes.educationDesc: Our culturally adapted sessions cover pregnancy wellbeing, birth preparation, infant feeding, and early parenting — all delivered with sensitivity to diverse cultural backgrounds and in multiple languages.
programmes.supportDesc: We provide continued postnatal support to ensure every mother feels confident, cared for, and connected to her community during the crucial weeks and months after birth.
programmes.multilingualDesc: All programmes are delivered with professional interpretation support in Arabic, Somali, Ukrainian, Farsi, Tigrinya, Kurdish, and English. We ensure language is never a barrier to accessing quality care.
programmes.partnersDesc: Our programmes are accessible only through verified referral partners — including NHS teams, midwives, health visitors, English Plus, Bridge Plus, New Routes, local churches, and mosques.

communitySupport.introDesc: Go Nurture Initiative CIC works hand-in-hand with a network of trusted community organisations, faith groups, and healthcare professionals across Norfolk to ensure every vulnerable mother receives the support she needs.
communitySupport.partnersDesc: We work with a wide range of experienced partners who share our commitment to supporting vulnerable women. Our referral network includes healthcare professionals, community organisations, and faith-based groups who are already trusted by the communities we serve.

howItWorks.introDesc: Go Nurture Initiative CIC provides free, culturally adapted perinatal education through a secure referral-led model. Here is how the process works — from the first referral to ongoing community support.
howItWorks.step1Desc: A healthcare professional, midwife, health visitor, or community organisation identifies a vulnerable woman who would benefit from our programme. They submit a secure referral through our partner portal with her consent.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Our team reviews the referral and places the woman into one of three annual cohorts. Each cohort supports up to 10 women, ensuring personalised, culturally adapted care throughout the journey.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Women receive comprehensive perinatal education, birth preparation, and postnatal support — all delivered in a safe, welcoming, multilingual environment with professional interpretation in Arabic, Somali, Ukrainian, Farsi, Tigrinya, Kurdish, and English.
howItWorks.step4Desc: After birth, mothers continue to receive postnatal support sessions, peer connection opportunities, and ongoing access to our community network — ensuring no one is left alone during the crucial early months of motherhood.
